name: Phoenix
first: First confirmation of water ice in the Martian arctic regolith; first soft propulsive Mars landing since Viking 2
description: Phoenix was salvaged from the cancelled Mars Surveyor 2001 program — flight hardware in storage for six years, reassembled and retargeted to the Martian north polar plains. The name was chosen literally. Landed 2008-05-25 at 68.22°N, 234.25°E on Vastitas Borealis, further north than any prior surface mission. Within days the robotic arm scraped through topsoil and exposed bright white ice that visibly sublimated on camera over four sols — direct confirmation of subsurface water ice in the Martian arctic. Detected perchlorates in the regolith and observed snow falling from clouds. Mission ended 2008-11-02 as solar power fell below operational threshold at the onset of Mars winter; the lander was never expected to survive the polar night.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Delta II 7925-9.5 from Cape Canaveral LC-17A.

events.label: TCM-6
events.note: Final pre-EDL trim 21 hours before entry.

events.label: EDL
events.note: Aeroshell, supersonic parachute, twelve hydrazine retro-rockets — Viking-style propulsive descent.

events.label: TOUCHDOWN
events.note: Soft landing at 68.22°N, 234.25°E — northernmost Mars surface mission.

events.label: ICE EXPOSED
events.note: Arm scrapes through topsoil. Bright white ice sublimates on camera over 4 sols.

events.label: MISSION END
events.note: 2008-11-02. Mars winter; solar power below operations threshold.
